data.name: Melaniel
data.long_meaning: The name Melaniel is derived from the Hebrew words 'melach' (dark) and 'el' (God). In the Bible, there are several figures with this name, each representing different aspects of God's character. In the Old Testament, Melaniel is a variant of the name Melchizedek, meaning 'king of righteousness'. In the New Testament, Melaniel is a name given to the angel Gabriel when he appears to the Blessed Virgin Mary to announce the birth of Jesus Christ. Thus, the name Melaniel signifies a connection to the divine, representing both the darkness of God's mysteries and the light of His revelation.
data.spiritual_meaning: A name signifying a deep connection to the divine, representing both the darkness of God's mysteries and the light of His revelation.
data.numerology_meaning: Melaniel is a name with a strong and independent energy. People with this name are natural born leaders and are often very self-confident and determined. They are not afraid to take risks and are always looking for new adventures.

data.spiritual_significance: As mentioned, the name Melaniel holds spiritual significance through its biblical origins. It represents the mystery and complexity of God, with the darkness alluding to the depths of His wisdom, while the 'el' root speaks to His divine nature. The name also highlights the angel Gabriel's essential role in the annunciation of Jesus Christ, emphasizing the significance of spiritual guidance, faith, and the divine plan.

She is said to have married a Roman soldier named Meleager and together they had a son named Rufus, who would later become a noted saint in the Catholic Church.

Another reference in the 'Golden Legend' tells the story of Melaniel as a Christian princess during the time of the Saracen invasions in Europe. She is said to have disguised herself as a man and led an army of Crusaders against the Saracens, outwitting and defeating them. After the battle, she was revealed to be a woman and was taken into the care of the Crusade leader, Baldwin III.
